# dsh-auto-rename

**Automatic conversation naming for DeepSeek Harness.**
Titles name themselves, refresh as the conve

rsation grows, and the rename dialog streams
AI suggestions.
English · 中文
## Features

**Names the conversation, and keeps up with it.** The first human message gets an AI title;
after th

at, every new message re-reads the recent ones and refreshes it, so the title follows
a topic that h

as moved on. Turn "Refresh title as the conversation grows" off and it goes back
to naming the first

message once. A manual rename pins the title either way, so it is never
rewritten under your hands.

**Suggests titles when you rename.** The **AI Name** button sits at the top of the conversation
page
. Its dialog looks and behaves like DSH's native rename window, with three extra things:
| Streaming candidates | Suggestions arrive one at a time (NDJSON), each revealed by a 500 ms left-t

o-right sweep |
| One-click apply | Click a chip to fill the input; **Regenerate** for a fresh set |
| Native feel | Enter confirms, Esc closes, and Enter during IME composition never submits by mista
ative feel | Enter confirms, Esc closes, and Enter during IME composition never submits by mistake |

**Uses a model you choose.** Naming follows the conversation's main model by default, or pins a
chea

per one. The dropdown is built from the host's `remote.session.modelCatalog()`, which
enumerates pro

viders one by one and drops those that return nothing — so every entry is a model
the host has actua
lly authenticated and can really call.

**Reasoning, handled for you.** A title needs three or four words, but a reasoning model spends
the

budget thinking first — the same `max_tokens` the answer draws from. So four things happen
automatic

t thinking first — the same `max_tokens` the answer draws from. So four things happen
automatically:
| Off when it can be | The model's own switch-off level is sent when it declares one (named `off` on

some gateways, `none` on others; only declared levels are ever trusted) |
| Lowest level when it ca
n't | Otherwise the lowest effort the model itself declares. Some gateways silently ignore an undecl

ared level instead of erroring, so a hand-typed level just makes the UI lie |
| A bigger cap for rea
soning models | Thinking that eats the budget returns an empty title; measured on one reasoning mode
l, thinking ran 325–3172 tokens, so reasoning models get 4096 (the schema ceiling). The cap only bou
nds generation and returns at `stop`, so it does not slow anything down — the timeout is the real gu

and returns at `stop`, so it does not slow anything down — the timeout is the real guard |

The package declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, so installing it also inserts `dsh-auto-rename` into
the pr

ofile's bundle stack **and disables the built-in `session-title-llm` row from dsh-base**.
That secon

d part is required: `SessionTitleService.register()` accepts exactly one provider
globally, so if th
e built-in row registers first, this plugin's registration throws.
Restart DSH afterwards. Client-side changes hot-reload; host-side changes need the restart.
## Settings

Open the **AI Name** dialog and click the gear in its title row, left of the close button. The
panel

expands inside the same dialog. Edits are staged in a draft and written only when you
press **Save*
*; an empty field means "use the default".
| Field | Default | Notes |
| Refresh title as the conversation grows | on | On: every new message re-reads the recent ones and

refreshes. Off: the first message is named once. Suggestions keep working either way |
| Naming mode

l | Follow main model | Lists only models the host has authenticated and can currently list |
| Reas
oning level | auto | The levels offered are the ones **this model declares**; auto = switch it off i

f possible, otherwise the lowest |
| Suggestions | 3 | Candidates fetched per dialog open (1–5) |
|
Output limit (tokens) | 256 | Per-generation cap (8–4096); raised to 4096 automatically when the mod

el thinks |
| Timeout (ms) | 60000 | Longest wait for one generated title (1000–600000). A retry get

s its own full budget, so the worst case is twice this |
| Title width (CJK characters) | 12 | **The
only length knob** (1–400); longer output is truncated |

If the host has no remote assembled, or listing fails, the model row falls back to manual
**Provider

** / **Model** fields. They must be filled in pairs: a half-set route logs a warning
[该节后续省略]
## How it works

**It reads only what you typed.** Neither path looks at assistant replies: automatic naming
takes th

e six most recent human messages (only the first one is ever scheduled when the refresh
toggle is of

f), suggestions take the three most recent ones, so both describe the topic in
progress. Each messag

e is clipped to `maxInputBytes` (default 4096) before it reaches the model,
because the official sha
red implementation throws on oversized input.

**Length is measured in display width, not characters.** One CJK character costs 2 half-width
units,

everything else — spaces included — costs 1. The budget is `Title width × 2`, so the
default `12` a

llows 12 Chinese characters or 24 Latin characters including spaces, roughly
3–4 words. One knob gov

erns both scripts; there is no separate word count for English, because
word lengths vary too much f
or a count to mean anything.

The official shared implementation still wants a `targetWords` value (prompt-only, never
truncating)

, so it is derived from the same budget at ~6 units per word — `12` yields `4`. That
keeps the model
's target close to the hard cut instead of writing long and being trimmed.

**Truncation avoids mangling words.** A cut landing mid-word falls back to the previous space,
so yo

u never get `sessio`. When there is no space to fall back to — a `provider/model` route, a
URL — the
title is left alone: slightly too wide beats a broken word.
Why the plugin has to truncate at all

The official caller passes `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` as the truncation argument of
`normalizeSession

Title` — that is, no truncation whatsoever. The host does enforce a
`maxTitleBytes` ceiling (80 byte

s ≈ 26 CJK characters), but it is far too loose to keep titles
short. So "not too long" is this plug

in's job, and the practical ceiling of the width knob sits
below the host's byte limit.
